subject: Canary client handshake metadata mismatch — flag/diagnostic request
messages:
From: Danielle Park <danielle@photonhealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-07T09:12:00Z
Subject: Observed metadata mismatch from mobile SDK during canary

Hi Chloe,

We started a small canary for our mobile app against the Redwood canary endpoint this morning and are seeing requests routed to a generic model variant instead of our tenant-pinned variant. From our side it looks like the client is sending the correct metadata (x-client-id and x-tenant), but the runtime occasionally shows the keys as missing or lowercased in the logs, which triggers route fallback.

Attached are a compressed set of our client logs and an extracted header capture (client_capture.headers.txt) showing a couple of the failing requests. The behavior is intermittent (roughly 1:200 requests) and correlates with short bursts of reconnects from the mobile SDK.

Example snippet from our capture (sensitive fields redacted):

--- capture start ---
GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: canary.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
x-client-id: PH-ABC-123
x-tenant: photon-prod
User-Agent: PhotonMobile/3.4.1

--- server-observed header for same request ---
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
user-agent: photonmobile/3.4.1

As you can see, the two metadata headers are missing when the runtime logs the request. We suspect a handshake/streaming race where metadata sometimes gets dropped.

Can your team advise on:
- Whether Redwood has any known behavior that normalizes/drops custom metadata during handshake or stream resumption
- If there's a quick escape hatch (feature flag) we can enable to force strict binding of client-supplied metadata to the routing decision
- Any additional capture or instrumentation you need from us

We can keep the canary running and provide packet-level captures if that helps.

Thanks,
Danielle
Danielle Park
Platform Engineer, Photon Health

Attachments: photon_logs_0607.tar.gz, client_capture.headers.txt

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Park <danielle@photonhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-07T10:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed metadata mismatch from mobile SDK during canary

Danielle,

Thanks for the detailed capture and repro notes — this is exactly the type of field report we want to catch early. I pinged Sean, Logan, and Marissa so we can triage quickly.

Quick answers up front:
- We do lowercase header keys in some parts of the pipeline for canonicalization, but we don't intentionally drop user-supplied x-* metadata.
- There is no tenant-level flag currently exposed to force "strict binding" of client-supplied metadata; it's a runtime switch we've discussed for routing stability.

Sean — can you do an initial read of the logs and determine if the drop pattern matches reconnect timing? Logan — can you weigh in on whether we can flip a per-tenant flag in canary to treat x-client-id/x-tenant as authoritative during routing?

Danielle, if you can also send a small pcap with the timing around reconnects that would be helpful. We're going to treat this as P1 for the canary tenant until we understand impact.

I'll coordinate a short call if we need to watch a live repro.

— Chloe
Chloe Martin
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Danielle Park <danielle@photonhealth.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-07T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed metadata mismatch from mobile SDK during canary

Chloe / Danielle — 

I pulled the attached server logs from our canary nodes and correlated timestamps with the header captures you sent. High level notes:
- The dropped headers line up with keepalive/reconnect spikes on the client (same minute).
- When the client reconnects, we observe a short window where the connection-level handshake hasn't fully applied the downstream metadata to the routing context; subsequent tokens get the right routing.

Temporary mitigations we can try:
1) Increase handshake logging and add early-kv dumps for failing requests (no runtime change, just additional logging).
2) Short term feature: expose a per-tenant "strict-handshake-binding" flag that forces routing to consult the raw initial metadata packet rather than the normalized context if present. This is a small runtime guard (~2 dev days + canary rollout) but will reduce fallbacks.
3) Long term: upgrade the client handshake to v2 that includes a metadata checksum so partial handshakes are detectable. That is a larger effort (client + runtime) and would be scoped Q4.

I attached a tiny capture (server_quick_capture.txt) showing an example request where we replay headers and the routing decision. If Photon wants, we can enable increased logging this afternoon and then turn on the strict flag for your canary only.

Sean

--- server_quick_capture.txt (attached) ---
RequestID: rq_74f2
ObservedHeaders: user-agent: photonmobile/3.4.1
RoutingVariant: default-generic
ExpectedHeaders: x-client-id: PH-ABC-123, x-tenant: photon-prod

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Danielle Park <danielle@photonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-08T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed metadata mismatch from mobile SDK during canary

Thanks for the repro materials. Quick technical summary from runtime side:

- We canonicalize header keys in the front proxy layer and then populate a routing context object. The canonicalization alone shouldn't drop headers, but if a streaming handshake completes in multiple frames there is a race where the routing decision is taken before the second frame (carrying x-client-id) is applied to the context.
- The race is most likely in our current streaming handshake path where we accept request frames and start scheduling before the full metadata is atomically merged.

Options:
A) Short-term (recommended for canary): implement a per-tenant toggle "strict-handshake-binding" that defers routing until the handshake completes OR forces routing to use literal headers when present. This is a conservative runtime change — estimated 2 dev days + 1 day testing + staged canary rollout. No client changes required.

B) Diagnostics-only: enable granular handshake tracing for your canary to capture the exact frame boundaries. This is low risk but will produce high-volume logs for a short window.

C) Long-term: handshake v2 with metadata checksum and atomic merge. Requires client SDK update (Photon) and runtime changes; target Q4.

If Photon is OK with A, we can schedule the patch for next-week canary rollout. We will need: list of canary tenant ids, a time window (we prefer low-traffic 2–4 hour window), and sign-off from Product for the temporary flag.

Logan
Principal Architect, Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Danielle Park <danielle@photonhealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-08T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed metadata mismatch from mobile SDK during canary

Team —

Thanks for the clear options. From a product/roadmap perspective I support path A as a temporary engineering control with path C as the durable fix. Action items and asks:
- Chloe, please confirm Photon will accept a short maintenance window for a canary patch next week.
- Logan / Eng: estimate the impact on the rollout schedule and whether QA needs additional test harnesses (I assume yes). Please provide a short PR/rollout plan by EOD Friday.
- Legal / Sales: if we flip tenant-level routing semantics temporarily we should note this in the canary-change log and confirm there are no SLA impacts for Photon.

If we can get Photon approval today, I'll prioritize the change and coordinate the canary window.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Danielle Park <danielle@photonhealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-09T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Observed metadata mismatch from mobile SDK during canary

Chloe / team —

Thanks — Photon is happy to proceed with option A as a temporary fix. We can provide packet captures and an exact list of canary tenant IDs. Preference would be to enable the strict flag only in our canary region (us-west-2) to limit blast radius.

Proposed window: Tuesday 2028-06-13, 02:00–04:00 UTC (low traffic). ETA ask: can you confirm a timeline for code + QA + canary rollout? If you can enable increased logging first we will keep sending captures while we wait for the flag.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on this.

Best,
Danielle
Danielle Park
Platform Engineer, Photon Health
